evidence: src/domain/product.ts: `interface Product { id: string; name: string; stock: number; }` and `interface CatalogueProduct { id: string; name: string; stock: number; }` are identical duplicate abstractions
src/domain/product.ts createProduct: `if (!id.trim()) throw new DomainError("Product id is required")`
src/domain/order.ts createOrder: `if (!item.productId.trim()) throw new DomainError("Product id is required")` repeats the product-id rule
src/domain/order.ts createOrder: `if (!id) throw new DomainError("Order id is required")` uses a different (non-trim) id check than the product rule
src/domain/order.ts: `import { DomainError } from "./product"` - the shared module error type is declared in product.ts rather than in a module-wide place
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The two files share one concern, the order/product domain, but the module does not keep its rules and abstractions in one place. product.ts declares two structurally identical product types, Product and CatalogueProduct, so the product concept is modelled twice. The rule that a product id is required (non-blank, checked with trim()) is written separately in createProduct and in createOrder's item loop, so it is duplicated instead of living in one place. Id validation is also inconsistent: createOrder checks the order id with `!id`, while createProduct and the item check use `!x.trim()`. Finally, the shared DomainError class is declared in product.ts, so order.ts depends on the product file for a cross-cutting module abstraction. That blurs the boundary between the two files.

violations.message: CatalogueProduct is a structural duplicate of Product (id, name, stock), so the product concept is modelled twice in the module.
createOrder writes its own copy of the 'Product id is required' check (`!item.productId.trim()`) instead of reusing the product-id rule in createProduct, so the invariant lives in two places.
Order id validation uses `!id` while product id validation uses `!id.trim()`, so id validation is inconsistent across the module.
The module-wide DomainError class is declared in the product file, so order.ts depends on product.ts for a shared abstraction that does not belong to products.
